title: Intra-lymph Node Injection of Biodegradable Polymer Particles
protocol: Combine DOPC, DSPE-PEG, and DOTAP lipids at a 60:20:20 molar ratio in a 7 ml glass vial.
Transfer 242.9 μl of DOPC into the vial using a 2 ml glass serological pipette.
Transfer 287.4 μl of DSPE-PEG into the vial using a 2 ml glass serological pipette.
Transfer 71.9 μl of DOTAP into the vial using a 2 ml glass serological pipette.
Dry lipids under a gentle stream of nitrogen gas for 10 min.
Dissolve 80 mg of PLGA in 5 ml of dichloromethane to generate a 16 mg/ml polymer stock solution.
Add 5 ml of polymer solution to the vial containing dried lipids, cap and vortex for 30 sec.
Begin sonicating the organic phase containing polymer, lipid, and other water-insoluble cargo on ice at 12 W using a sonicator.
Create the water-in-oil (w/o) emulsion by adding 500 μl of distilled H2O or H2O containing 1 mg of peptide, protein, or other water-soluble cargo.
Sonicate the organic phase containing polymer, lipid, and other water-insoluble cargo on ice at 14 W.
Add 500 µl of distilled H2O using a pipette to create the w/o emulsion.
Continue sonicating for 30 sec at 14 W on ice.
Pour the w/o emulsion into 40 ml of H2O in a 150 ml beaker and sonicate for 5 min at 16 W on ice.
Gently rock the vial up and down and side to side around the sonicator tip.
Add a magnetic stir bar, transfer the beaker to a stir plate, and allow the w/o/w emulsion to stir overnight.
Pour the emulsion through a 40 µm Nylon mesh cell strainer into a 50 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge particles for 5 min at 5,000 x g for microparticles or 5 min at 24,000 x g for nanoparticles.
Decant supernatant and wash particles by resuspending in 1 ml of H₂O.
Transfer suspended particles to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 5,000 x g for microparticles or 5 min at 24,500 x g for nanoparticles.
Remove supernatant and resuspend particles in 1 ml H₂O.
Repeat the centrifugation step as described previously.
After washing, suspend particles in 1 ml H₂O for immediate use.
Lyophilize particles for extended storage if not using immediately.
Preweigh an empty 20 ml glass vial.
Add 100 µl of particle suspension to the preweighed vial and mix thoroughly.
Lyophilize or dry particles under a gentle stream of nitrogen.
Weigh the vial containing dried polymer after drying.
Determine particle yield by subtracting original weight of vial from mass of vial with dried particles.
Calculate overall particle yield by multiplying particle mass in vial by dilution factor.
Determine percent yield by dividing particle mass by maximum theoretical input mass and multiply by 100%.
Clean the supplied cuvette-style glass fraction cell by filling it with deionized water and wiping with a cotton-tipped swab.
Transfer 10 ml of distilled H₂O to the cleaned fraction cell, add magnetic micro stir bar.
Load the fraction cell into the cell mount of the particle size analyzer.
Adjust the magnetic stirring speed in the particle analyzer to achieve complete mixing in the fraction cell.
Close the compartment door of the particle size analyzer.
Align the lasers to the fraction cell using the instrument software interface.
Record a baseline reading with the fraction cell containing only distilled H₂O.
Pipette the original particle suspension up and down with a micropipette to mix.
Pipette 10 µl of particle suspension into the fraction cell.
Ensure the volume of particle sample added to the cell generates signal strength in the appropriate range as indicated on the instrument software interface.
Close the compartment door of the particle size analyzer.
Measure particle size using a refractive index of 1.60 for PLGA.
Calculate particle diameter using a number basis through the software interface.
Pipette particle suspension up and down with micropipette to mix.
Dilute particle suspension to 1 mg/ml in deionized water.
Prepare a microscope slide by adding 3 µl of diluted particle suspension.
Mount a coverslip at a 45° angle on the prepared microscope slide.
Place the slide on the microscope stage and image using appropriate filter sets for each fluorescent cargo.
Prepare a 0.1% (w/v) solution of tracer dye by dissolving 10 mg of dye powder in 10 ml of distilled water.
Sterilize the dye solution using a 0.2 μm syringe filter and transfer it into a glass vial.
Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane according to an IACUC approved animal protocol.
Perform a toe pinch reflex test to evaluate the depth of anesthesia.
Monitor breathing rate to ensure a respiratory rate of approximately 100-140 breaths per minute.
Shave hair at the base of the tail and hindquarter using clippers while the mouse is anesthetized.
Remove hair from the ventral side of the animal and laterally around to the dorsal side just above the joint of the hind leg (hip).
Transfer 10 μl of dye solution into a microcentrifuge tube using a micropipette.
Aspirate the entire 10 μl of dye solution into a 31G needle attached to a 1 ml syringe.
Inject 10 μl of dye solution subcutaneously on each side of the tail base where the hair was clipped, reloading between injections.
Apply a mild depilatory cream via cotton swabs to remove remaining hair from the area in between the hind thigh and abdomen.
Allow the depilatory cream to incubate on the skin for 3 minutes.
Wet gloved hand with warm water and gently rub the depilatory cream into the skin.
Remove depilatory cream by wetting gloved hand with warm H2O and rubbing tail base and hindquarter until excess depilatory is removed.
Wet a soft cloth or paper towel with warm H2O and wipe lower portion of mouse in a single motion to remove residual depilary cream.
Allow the mouse to recover under a heat lamp.
Anesthetize the mouse using isoflurane according to an IACUC approved animal protocol.
Examine the mouse to confirm tracer dye drainage into each inguinal lymph node.
Resuspend particles in distilled H2O at desired injection concentration.
Transfer 10 µl of particle solution into a microcentrifuge tube using a micropipette.
Aspirate the entire 10 µl of particle solution into a 31G insulin needle attached to a 1 ml syringe.
Tighten skin around LN using thumb, index finger, and middle finger to pull skin taut for controlled injection volume placement.
Approach the LN with the needle at a 90° angle to the skin.
Penetrate the skin over the dyed LN to a depth of 1 mm.
Slowly inject the entire volume.
Observe the LN volume through the skin during injection.
Confirm injection by visible LN enlargement.
Allow the mouse to recover under a heat lamp.
Return the mouse to holding or conduct additional testing.
